meta.editorialPolicy: Every breakthrough must link to a primary peer-reviewed journal, government registry (FDA / ClinicalTrials.gov), formal proof repository (Lean 4 / Mathlib), or official research institution release—and include honest limitations.

verified.label: Verified / Deployed
verified.description: Peer-reviewed in a leading journal (Nature, Science, NEJM, Cell), machine-checked in a proof assistant (Lean 4), FDA-authorized, or operating at scale.

trial.label: Clinical Trial / Replicated
trial.description: Advancing through registered human clinical trials (ClinicalTrials.gov) or independently replicated in lab/field studies awaiting full deployment.

milestone.label: Frontier Milestone
milestone.description: Verified benchmark breakthrough, novel mathematical bound, or institutional result that establishes a new scientific capability.

domains.label: Medicine & Biology
domains.description: Protein folding, antibiotic discovery, AI-designed clinical drugs, genetics, and FDA-authorized diagnostic tools.

domains.label: Mathematics & Proofs
domains.description: Machine-checked Lean 4 proofs, faster algorithms, open-problem progress, and Olympiad-level mathematical reasoning.

domains.label: Science, Weather & Energy
domains.description: Extreme-weather forecasting, novel battery & catalyst materials, fusion plasma control, and clean-grid optimization.

domains.label: Accessibility & Daily Life
domains.description: Speech-restoring brain interfaces, visual aids for blind users, 200-language translation, tutoring trials, and clinician time savings.

events.title: Halicin: First Broad-Spectrum Antibiotic Discovered by Deep Learning
events.plainHeadline: AI discovered a new antibiotic that kills drug-resistant bacteria
events.summary: MIT researchers trained a neural network to screen 100+ million chemical compounds in days, identifying Halicin—a structurally novel molecule that killed drug-resistant bacteria including C. difficile and A. baumannii in mouse models.
events.whyItMatters: Antibiotic resistance kills over 1.2 million people per year globally, while traditional pharma pipelines have struggled to find new antibiotic classes for decades.
events.caveats: Halicin proved the AI discovery method in lab and animal models, but still requires years of safety optimization and human clinical trials before hospital use.

events.title: AlphaFold 2 Solves the 50-Year Protein Folding Grand Challenge
events.plainHeadline: AI solved the 50-year puzzle of how proteins fold
events.summary: At CASP14, AlphaFold 2 predicted 3D atomic protein structures from amino-acid sequences with accuracy rivaling years-long X-ray crystallography and cryo-EM experiments.
events.whyItMatters: Knowing a protein's 3D shape is foundational to understanding disease mechanisms and designing targeted medicines—work that previously took months to years per protein now takes minutes.
events.caveats: AlphaFold 2 predicts static single-chain snapshots well, but dynamic conformational changes and disordered proteins remain active research areas.

events.title: AI Helps Mathematicians Discover New Theorems in Knot & Representation Theory
events.plainHeadline: AI helped mathematicians spot and prove new theorems
events.summary: Mathematicians used machine learning attribution techniques to detect unexpected patterns across high-dimensional mathematical objects, leading to two new proven theorems linking algebraic and geometric knot invariants.
events.whyItMatters: Demonstrated that AI can act as an intuition amplifier for human mathematicians—spotting subtle structural links across millions of examples before humans prove them rigorously.
events.caveats: Human mathematicians still formulated the final conjectures and wrote the rigorous proofs; AI acted as a pattern-finding collaborator rather than an autonomous prover.

events.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning Controls Superheated Fusion Plasma in Real Time
events.plainHeadline: AI learned to steer super-hot fusion plasma
events.summary: A single AI controller dynamically adjusted 19 magnetic coils 10,000 times per second inside the real TCV tokamak reactor, sculpting novel plasma shapes including 'droplets' and 'snowflakes' previously hard to stabilize.
events.whyItMatters: Stable magnetic confinement is one of the core engineering barriers to clean, abundant nuclear fusion energy.
events.caveats: Achieving net commercial fusion electricity still depends on reactor materials, tritium breeding, and scaling from experimental tokamaks to power plants.

events.title: Open-Source AI Translation Expands Across 200 World Languages
events.plainHeadline: Free AI translation now covers 200 languages
events.summary: No Language Left Behind (NLLB-200) released open-source models able to translate directly between 200 languages—including dozens of African, Asian, and Indigenous languages previously ignored by commercial translation.
events.whyItMatters: Opens medical guidance, Wikipedia knowledge, education, and cross-border communication to billions of speakers of underserved languages.
events.caveats: Translation accuracy on very low-resource languages still trails high-resource pairs like English–Spanish and requires human review in medical or legal settings.
metrics: 44% BLEU quality gain on low-resource pairs

events.title: AlphaFold Database Opens 200 Million+ Protein Structures Free to All Scientists
events.plainHeadline: Nearly every known protein structure, free for all scientists
events.summary: EMBL-EBI and DeepMind expanded the open AlphaFold Protein Structure Database to over 200 million predicted structures—covering nearly every cataloged protein across 1 million species, free for any lab worldwide.
events.whyItMatters: Over 2 million researchers in 190+ countries now use the open database daily for malaria vaccines, plastic-degrading enzymes, crop resilience, and rare genetic diseases.
events.caveats: Predicted structures include confidence scores (pLDDT); experimental verification is still required before clinical drug manufacturing.

events.title: AlphaTensor Discovers Faster Matrix Multiplication Algorithms After 50 Years
events.plainHeadline: AI found faster ways to do core computer math
events.summary: Framing algorithm design as a single-player game, AlphaTensor rediscovered Strassen's 1969 algorithm from scratch and beat the 50-year record for 4×4 matrix multiplication in modular arithmetic (47 multiplications vs. 49).
events.whyItMatters: Matrix multiplication sits at the core of computer graphics, scientific simulations, signal processing, and AI compute itself—faster algorithms save electricity across billions of devices.
events.caveats: The 47-multiplication breakthrough applied to finite field (mod 2) arithmetic rather than standard real numbers—a gap later tackled by AlphaEvolve in 2025.

events.title: Real-Time Multimodal Vision AI Deployed for Blind & Low-Vision Users
events.plainHeadline: AI describes the world for blind and low-vision people
events.summary: Be My Eyes launched 'Be My AI', giving hundreds of thousands of blind and low-vision people instant conversational descriptions of medication labels, appliances, menus, transit signs, and surroundings from a phone camera.
events.whyItMatters: Provides 24/7 independent access to everyday visual information—complementing human volunteers with instant, private assistance.
events.caveats: Vision models can still misread tiny or blurry text; users are advised to verify critical items like prescription dosages with a human volunteer or pharmacist.

events.title: AI Discovers Abaucin to Target Hospital Superbug Acinetobacter baumannii
events.plainHeadline: AI found a drug against a deadly hospital superbug
events.summary: Researchers screened ~7,500 molecules experimentally to train an AI model that then narrowed 6,680 candidates in under two hours—discovering Abaucin, which selectively destroys WHO-priority hospital pathogen A. baumannii.
events.whyItMatters: Unlike broad-spectrum antibiotics that wipe out beneficial gut bacteria and fuel resistance, Abaucin is narrow-spectrum—sparing helpful microbes while killing a deadly ICU pathogen.
events.caveats: Validated in lab cultures and mouse wound infections; still needs medicinal chemistry refinement and human clinical trials.

sources.label: Nature Chemical Biology Paper (Liu et al., 2023)

events.title: AI Brain-Computer Interfaces Restore Speech at 62–78 Words/Min for Paralyzed Patients
events.plainHeadline: Brain implants plus AI let paralyzed patients speak again
events.summary: Two landmark back-to-back Nature papers showed neural-network speech decoders translating cortical brain signals into audible speech and facial avatars at 62–78 words per minute—approaching natural conversation speed (160 wpm).
events.whyItMatters: Restores human voice and independence to people who lost speech from ALS or brainstem stroke—more than 3× faster than prior eye-tracking or BCI records.
events.caveats: Currently requires surgical brain implants in small clinical trials (NCT00912041 / NCT03698149); long-term wireless hardware durability is still being engineered.

events.title: AlphaMissense Maps 71 Million Human Genetic Mutations for Rare-Disease Diagnosis
events.plainHeadline: AI mapped 71 million genetic mutations to speed rare-disease diagnosis
events.summary: Prior to AlphaMissense, clinicians knew the effect of only ~0.1% of possible single-letter human missense mutations. AlphaMissense scored all 71 million possible variants, classifying 89% as likely benign or likely pathogenic.
events.whyItMatters: Rare genetic disease families often endure a 5+ year 'diagnostic odyssey.' Open variant predictions help clinical geneticists pinpoint root mutations dramatically faster.
events.caveats: Predictions are decision-support tools and cannot replace clinical geneticist evaluation or confirmatory lab testing.

events.title: GraphCast Outperforms Gold-Standard 10-Day Global Weather Forecasts in <1 Minute
events.plainHeadline: AI beats the best 10-day weather forecast, in under a minute
events.summary: Trained on 40 years of ERA5 historical weather data, GraphCast outperformed ECMWF's flagship HRES physics simulation on 90% of 1,380 verification targets—running on a single TPU in under a minute instead of hours on a supercomputer.
events.whyItMatters: Faster, sharper cyclone track and extreme-temperature predictions give coastal towns, farmers, and grid operators crucial extra days to save lives and protect infrastructure.
events.caveats: Trained on historical reanalysis datasets, so unprecedented climate extremes outside historical distributions still benefit from hybrid physics-AI checks.

events.title: GNoME Predicts 380,000+ Stable Novel Crystals for Batteries, Solar & Superconductors
events.plainHeadline: AI discovered 380,000 new materials for batteries and solar
events.summary: Graph Networks for Materials Exploration (GNoME) predicted 2.2 million crystal structures—including 380,000 energetically stable materials, expanding humanity's catalog of known stable inorganic crystals nearly 10×—with 736 independently synthesized in labs.
events.whyItMatters: Accelerates the hunt for safer solid-state lithium batteries, cheaper solar absorbers, and carbon-capture catalysts—all shared openly via the Materials Project.
events.caveats: Independent crystallographers noted that some predicted materials are close variants of known compounds and synthesizing commercially scalable materials remains hard lab work.

events.title: FunSearch Uses LLMs + Automated Verifiers to Discover New Math Constructions
events.plainHeadline: AI discovered new math constructions, checked by computer

bigStat.label: record on an open math problem

events.summary: By pairing an LLM with a strict programmatic evaluator that rejects hallucinations, FunSearch discovered the largest known cap sets in 8 dimensions—the first time an LLM produced a genuinely new verifiable discovery in an open math problem.
events.whyItMatters: Established the 'Generate + Formally Verify' blueprint: LLMs can brainstorm creatively while deterministic math verifiers guarantee 100% correctness.
events.caveats: Requires problems whose candidate solutions can be scored automatically by code; does not apply directly to abstract proofs without a verifier.
metrics: New record on 8D Cap Set problem

events.title: AlphaGeometry Solves Olympiad Geometry at Gold-Medalist Level
events.plainHeadline: AI solves Olympiad geometry like a gold medalist
events.summary: Combining a neural language model (trained on 100M synthetic proofs) with a symbolic deduction engine, AlphaGeometry solved 25 of 30 past International Mathematical Olympiad geometry problems within competition time limits.
events.whyItMatters: Proved neuro-symbolic AI can generate human-readable, step-by-step verified mathematical proofs rather than opaque guesses.
events.caveats: Limited specifically to Euclidean Olympiad geometry; algebra, combinatorics, and number theory required broader formal proof systems.

events.title: AlphaFold 3 Models All Life Molecules: Proteins, DNA, RNA & Drug Ligands Together
events.plainHeadline: AI now models how drugs bind to DNA, RNA and proteins
events.summary: AlphaFold 3 extended atomic-scale structure prediction beyond single proteins to how proteins interact with DNA, RNA, antibodies, and small-molecule drug candidates—improving drug-binding accuracy by 50%+ over physics docking tools.
events.whyItMatters: Directly addresses how real medicines work inside living cells, helping academic labs and drug designers screen therapeutic interactions before costly wet-lab synthesis.
events.caveats: Initial release restricted commercial drug-ligand code; full academic source code and weights were released in Nov 2024 following researcher feedback.

events.title: Controlled Trials Show Pedagogical AI Tutors Double Learning Gains per Hour
events.plainHeadline: AI tutors doubled how much students learned per hour
events.summary: A Harvard introductory physics RCT found students using a guardrail-designed Socratic AI tutor learned more than twice as much in less time compared to active-learning lectures; a World Bank RCT in Nigeria saw ~2 years of learning gains in 6 weeks.
events.whyItMatters: One-on-one human tutoring is the gold standard in education but unaffordable for most families. Well-designed AI tutors can expand personalized help globally.
events.caveats: Unconstrained chatbots that simply give away answers can *harm* learning retention—pedagogical scaffolding and teacher oversight are essential. Newer evidence is mixed: a two-year randomized trial in 18 U.S. middle schools (NBER w35620, 2026) found math gains with an AI tutor were no larger than with the same practice platform without AI, and trials in Ghana and China found no effect.

sources.label: Harvard Physics AI Tutor Study (Scientific Reports / Preprint)
World Bank AI Tutoring Study in Nigeria

events.title: 40-Year-Old Busy Beaver Problem BB(5) Solved & Machine-Verified in Lean 4
events.plainHeadline: A 40-year-old math puzzle solved and computer-verified
events.summary: An open online collaboration proved that the maximum steps a halting 5-state Turing machine can take is exactly 47,176,870—verifying the entire massive case analysis automatically in the Lean 4 proof assistant.
events.whyItMatters: Proved that crowdsourced math + automated formal verification in Lean 4 can cleanly resolve decades-old theoretical computer science problems with zero human checking errors.
events.caveats: BB(6) is vastly harder and touches Collatz-like number-theory obstacles that remain well beyond current automation.

events.title: AlphaProof & AlphaGeometry 2 Reach IMO Silver-Medal Score with Formal Proofs
events.plainHeadline: AI earned a silver-medal score at the Math Olympiad
events.summary: Solving 4 of 6 problems on the 2024 International Mathematical Olympiad—including the hardest number-theory problem solved by only 5 human contestants—AlphaProof produced machine-verified Lean 4 proofs scoring 28/42 (1 point shy of gold).
events.whyItMatters: Marked the leap from narrow geometry to general Olympiad algebra and number theory backed by mathematical certainty via Lean 4.
events.caveats: Required days of compute on the hardest problem and manual human translation of problem statements into Lean syntax.

events.title: FDA Reaches 950+ Authorized AI/ML Medical Devices in U.S. Clinics
events.plainHeadline: The FDA has cleared 950+ AI tools for doctors
events.summary: The FDA's official public registry crossed 950 authorized AI/ML-enabled medical devices—powering rapid stroke clot alerts, mammography screening, diabetic retinopathy exams, colonoscopy polyp detection, and cardiac ultrasound.
events.whyItMatters: Shows AI isn't just lab demos: hundreds of regulated clinical tools are already deployed in U.S. hospitals catching strokes and cancers minutes or months earlier.
events.caveats: Most clearances come via the 510(k) pathway rather than large randomized mortality trials; ongoing post-market auditing across diverse patient demographics is critical.

sources.label: FDA Official AI/ML-Enabled Medical Devices List

events.title: GenCast Probabilistic AI Surpasses World's Best 15-Day Extreme Weather Model
events.plainHeadline: AI out-forecasts the world's best 15-day weather model
events.summary: A diffusion-based probabilistic weather model outperformed ECMWF's operational ENS ensemble on 97.2% of 1,320 targets out to 15 days—with dramatically better tropical cyclone paths, extreme heat/cold probabilities, and wind-power forecasts.
events.whyItMatters: Knowing the *probability* of extreme storms 10–15 days ahead lets emergency responders evacuate earlier and helps renewable grids balance wind and solar power reliably.
events.caveats: Requires assimilation of live satellite/radar observations from national weather agencies (NOAA, ECMWF)—it augments, rather than replaces, global weather observation networks.
metrics: Beat ECMWF ENS on 97.2% of targets

events.title: Multi-Agent 'AI Co-Scientist' Generates Wet-Lab Validated Biomedical Discoveries
events.plainHeadline: An AI co-scientist proposed ideas confirmed in real labs
events.organization: Google Research, Stanford & Imperial College London
events.summary: A multi-agent scientific reasoning system independently proposed novel drug-repurposing candidates for acute myeloid leukemia, epigenetic targets for liver fibrosis, and a bacterial gene-transfer mechanism that Imperial College biologists had spent years discovering independently.
events.whyItMatters: Demonstrates AI moving from pattern lookup to generating testable scientific hypotheses that hold up in physical laboratory experiments.
events.caveats: Early wet-lab and organoid validation is promising, but human clinical trials remain years away; peer review and independent lab replication are ongoing.
metrics: Days vs. years for hypothesis discovery

events.title: Hospital Ambient AI Scribes Cut Physician Charting Burnout in Multi-System Studies
events.plainHeadline: AI note-taking gives doctors back about an hour a day
events.organization: Kaiser Permanente, Stanford Medicine & Mass General Brigham
events.summary: Large-scale deployments across tens of thousands of clinicians showed ambient AI medical scribes saving ~1 hour of after-hours EHR documentation per doctor per day, significantly reducing clinician burnout and restoring eye contact with patients.
events.whyItMatters: Doctor burnout and administrative overload drive healthcare shortages and rushed visits—this is one of the fastest-adopted, measurable quality-of-life wins for both patients and doctors.
events.caveats: Clinicians must still proofread AI-generated notes for occasional omissions or hallucinations; cost-equity for small rural clinics remains a barrier.

sources.label: JAMA Network Open Ambient AI Study

events.title: AlphaEvolve Breaks 56-Year Strassen Matrix Record & Advances 50+ Open Math Problems
events.plainHeadline: AI broke a 56-year-old math record
events.summary: An evolutionary coding agent powered by Gemini models discovered an algorithm to multiply 4×4 complex-valued matrices in 48 scalar multiplications—the first improvement over Volker Strassen's 1969 algorithm—while improving best-known bounds on 20% of 50+ open math problems and cutting Google data-center compute usage by 0.7%.
events.whyItMatters: Bridges pure mathematical discovery with direct real-world energy efficiency: the exact same system improved a 1969 theorem, advanced the 11D kissing-number bound, and lowered live server power use.
events.caveats: Works best where automated evaluation functions can score candidate code/constructions rapidly; deeper conceptual proofs still require mathematicians and formal provers.

events.title: Aurora Foundation Model Forecasts Air Quality, Ocean Waves & Tropical Cyclones
events.plainHeadline: AI forecasts storms, air quality and ocean waves
events.summary: Published in Nature, Aurora demonstrated that a single pre-trained atmospheric foundation model can be fine-tuned to beat specialized operational physics models on 5-day global air-pollution forecasts, 10-day ocean wave heights, and 100% of 5-day tropical cyclone tracks across 7 agencies.
events.whyItMatters: Extends AI forecasting beyond temperature and rain to breathable air-quality alerts (PM2.5/wildfire smoke) and maritime safety—at orders-of-magnitude lower supercomputing cost.
events.caveats: Depends on high-quality Earth observation inputs and still requires domain-specific fine-tuning for localized microclimates.

events.title: Rentosertib: First Fully AI-Discovered Target & Drug Succeeds in Phase IIa Human Trial
events.plainHeadline: First fully AI-discovered drug succeeds in a human trial
events.summary: Published in Nature Medicine, Rentosertib (INS018_055)—whose biological target (TNIK) and novel molecular structure were both discovered by generative AI—met safety endpoints and improved lung function (FVC +98.4 mL vs. −20.3 mL placebo) in patients with fatal idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF).
events.whyItMatters: IPF is a progressive, lethal lung disease with median survival of 3–5 years. Rentosertib went from AI target discovery to human trials in ~18 months instead of the typical 4–5 years.
events.caveats: Phase IIa involved 71 patients over 12 weeks—larger, multi-year Phase IIb/III randomized trials are still required before potential FDA approval.

events.title: Frontier AI Models Achieve Gold-Medal Level (35/42) at the 2025 Math Olympiad
events.plainHeadline: AI reached gold-medal level at the Math Olympiad
events.summary: General-purpose reasoning models (Google DeepMind's Gemini Deep Think—officially certified by IMO coordinators—and OpenAI's experimental reasoning model graded by former IMO medalists) solved 5 of 6 problems on the 2025 IMO directly in natural language within the 4.5-hour human time limit.
events.whyItMatters: In just 12 months, AI jumped from specialized Lean-assisted silver (requiring days of compute) to general-purpose natural-language gold-medal proof writing at human competition speed.
events.caveats: Competition math problems are self-contained and known to have clean solutions; open research problems like the Riemann Hypothesis remain far harder and unverified until formally checked.

events.title: FDA Authorized AI Medical Devices Surpass 1,250+ Tools Across U.S. Healthcare
events.plainHeadline: FDA-cleared AI medical tools pass 1,250
events.summary: Annual FDA clearances of AI-enabled clinical devices continued climbing past 1,250 cumulative authorizations—expanding beyond radiology into cardiology, neurology, pathology, sepsis early warning, and autonomous diabetic eye screening.
events.whyItMatters: Represents a 20× expansion since 2018 in regulated clinical AI helping catch life-threatening conditions earlier across community and academic hospitals.
events.caveats: Clinical adoption still concentrates in larger health systems; transparency around training-data demographics and ongoing drift monitoring remains an active FDA focus.

events.title: Lean 4 Mathlib Crosses 200K+ Verified Theorems as AI Accelerates Erdős Formalization
events.plainHeadline: 200,000+ math theorems are now computer-checked
events.summary: The open-source Mathlib4 library surpassed 200,000 formally verified theorems while mathematicians paired frontier reasoning models with Lean 4 to auto-formalize literature and resolve several long-standing Erdős problems tracked on erdosproblems.com.
events.whyItMatters: Formal proof assistants eliminate AI hallucinations: when an AI proposes a proof and Lean's tiny kernel compiles it, mathematicians get 100% mathematical certainty.
events.caveats: Several early AI-assisted Erdős resolutions turned out to rediscover obscure existing literature rather than totally new techniques—highlighting the need for careful mathematical curation.

events.title: Grid-Scale AI Cuts Renewable Curtailment & Accelerates Transmission Interconnection
events.plainHeadline: AI squeezes more clean power out of existing power lines
events.organization: U.S. National Labs, Grid Operators & Clean-Energy Platforms
events.summary: Utilities and regional grid operators deployed AI-driven dynamic line rating, hyper-local solar/wind output forecasting, and automated interconnection study tools—unlocking additional gigawatts on existing power lines without waiting years for new steel towers.
events.whyItMatters: Directly ties AI's own energy footprint back to solutions: smarter forecasting reduces wasted wind/solar curtailment and helps clean power come online faster.
events.caveats: AI grid software improves utilization by ~10–30% on congested lines, but cannot replace physical high-voltage transmission buildouts needed for gigawatt AI loads.

sources.label: U.S. DOE AI for Grid Reliability & Energy

events.title: 100,000-Woman Randomized Trial: AI-Supported Mammography Misses Fewer Cancers
events.plainHeadline: In a trial of 100,000 women, AI-assisted mammogram reading missed fewer cancers
events.summary: Women in Sweden were randomized to AI-supported mammogram reading or standard double reading by two radiologists. The AI arm detected 81% of cancers at screening vs. 74%, had 12% fewer interval cancers (1.55 vs. 1.76 per 1,000) and 27% fewer aggressive-subtype cancers, with similar false-positive rates.
events.whyItMatters: It is randomized evidence that AI screening helps patients in the real world—catching more cancers earlier—not just a benchmark score.
events.caveats: One country and one AI system with experienced radiologists, and a human still read every scan; the lead author has industry ties.

events.title: Germany's National Weather Service Runs an AI Global Forecast Model Every Day
events.plainHeadline: Germany's national weather service now runs an AI global forecast every day

bigStat.label: AI forecasts at a national agency

events.summary: DWD's AICON global AI model became fully operational, running daily at 13 km resolution and matching the skill of DWD's physics model, especially for surface weather. ECMWF lists it alongside AI models run by Canada's and the U.S.'s national weather services.
events.whyItMatters: National forecasters now rely on AI in daily operations, not just research—faster, cheaper forecasts that help warn people about severe weather.
events.caveats: AICON supplements rather than replaces the physics model, and its performance write-up is a preprint, not yet peer reviewed.

events.title: People With Paralysis Type by Imagining Finger Movements With Near-Typist Accuracy
events.plainHeadline: People with paralysis typed by thinking about finger movements, almost error-free

bigStat.label: word error rate typing by thought

events.summary: A brain-computer interface decoded imagined finger movements so people with paralysis could type at up to 22 words per minute with a 1.6% word error rate. It was calibrated with as few as 30 sentences and used at home.
events.whyItMatters: Fast, accurate typing by thought could restore everyday communication for people who cannot move or speak, with far less setup than before.
events.caveats: Two participants, with the top figures from one of them; the devices are investigational.

events.title: Largest Real-World Study of AI Scribes Finds Modest Time Savings for Doctors
events.plainHeadline: AI note-taking gave doctors back a little time in the largest study yet

bigStat.label: less paperwork per 8 hours of care

events.organization: Mass General Brigham, UCSF & 3 other academic centers
events.summary: Across five academic centers (~1,800 users vs. 6,770 controls), ambient AI scribes cut documentation time by about 16 minutes per 8 hours of patient care (~10%), and users saw roughly one extra patient every two weeks.
events.whyItMatters: It is the largest real-world measurement of clinician time savings so far—an honest, measured gain rather than a vendor claim.
events.caveats: Not randomized, gains were modest, and after-hours charting did not change.

events.title: AI Co-Scientist's Drug-Repurposing Ideas Block Liver Fibrosis in Human Organoids
events.plainHeadline: An AI research assistant found existing drugs that fought liver scarring in lab tests
events.summary: In a Nature paper, Google's multi-agent AI co-scientist proposed repurposed drugs for liver fibrosis; two of its three candidates blocked fibrosis in human liver organoids, while neither of two expert-chosen drugs did. A companion Stanford study found vorinostat blocked 91% of a scarring response.
events.whyItMatters: It shows AI generating testable medical hypotheses that held up in the lab, which could shorten the path to new treatments.
events.caveats: Lab dishes only, with humans choosing candidates and running every experiment; human trials would still be needed.

events.title: Man With ALS Uses a Speech Brain Implant at Home for Two Years
events.plainHeadline: A man with ALS has used a brain implant at home for two years to talk and work

bigStat.label: words per minute, at home, for 2 years

events.summary: A participant with ALS used an AI speech brain-computer interface independently at home for over 3,800 hours, producing about 2 million words at an average of 56 words per minute with over 99% word accuracy in controlled tests, and also used it for computer work.
events.whyItMatters: It is the first evidence of a speech brain implant working independently in everyday life, giving a voice back to someone who lost it.
events.caveats: One participant, and the device is still investigational.

events.title: AI 'Double Neural Bypass' Helps a Paralyzed Man Feed Himself and Regain Touch
events.plainHeadline: A paralyzed man regained the ability to feed himself and feel touch in his hand
events.summary: AI decodes the participant's movement intentions to stimulate his muscles while sensors send touch back to his brain. After 35 weeks his right arm was 86% stronger, and many gains persisted even when stimulation stopped.
events.whyItMatters: It suggests AI-driven implants may help restore lost function, not just bypass an injury.
events.caveats: One participant, and the explanation that nerves 'rewired' remains an interpretation.

events.title: AI Cyclone Model Adds About a Day of Warning on Hurricane Track and Strength
events.plainHeadline: AI gives about one extra day of warning on where hurricanes will go
events.summary: Published in Nature and open-sourced, the model's 3-day forecasts match older models' 2-day skill on cyclone track and intensity, and it generates 1,000 scenarios per storm. The U.S. National Hurricane Center's 2025 verification report ranked DeepMind's model the top track performer.
events.whyItMatters: An extra day of warning means earlier evacuations and more time to protect people and property.
events.caveats: Headline accuracy comes from 2023–24 historical storms; official 2026-season verification is not yet published.
metrics: Top track model in NHC 2025 verification

events.title: AI Predicts and Prevents Fusion Plasma Instabilities in Real Time on DIII-D
events.plainHeadline: AI spotted and stopped fusion reactor instabilities before they formed
events.summary: On the DIII-D tokamak, AI models controlled heating, density and instability suppression in real time on a ~20 ms loop across five experiments, predicting a tearing instability about 200 ms ahead and preventing it.
events.whyItMatters: Future fusion power plants will need control faster than humans can manage; this shows AI can keep the plasma stable.
events.caveats: One machine and initial results, with no measured gain in fusion output.

events.title: AI-Discovered Lung-Fibrosis Drug Rentosertib Enters Phase III
events.plainHeadline: The AI-discovered lung drug that worked in a mid-stage trial is now in final testing
events.summary: The first patient was dosed in GENESIS-IPF-3 (NCT07687459), a 52-week placebo-controlled Phase III trial of 320 patients at 47 centers in China. In Phase IIa (Nature Medicine, 2025), lung capacity rose 98.4 mL on the drug vs. a 20.3 mL decline on placebo.
events.whyItMatters: AI-originated drugs are now reaching the trial stage that decides whether a medicine gets approved.
events.caveats: No Phase III results exist yet and approval is years away; the 'first generative-AI drug' framing is the company's own.

events.title: FDA's AI-Enabled Device List Passes 1,600 Authorized Tools
events.plainHeadline: The FDA has now cleared more than 1,600 AI tools to help doctors
events.summary: The FDA's official AI-enabled medical device list reports more than 1,600 authorized devices as of September 2026, most of them imaging tools used in radiology.
events.whyItMatters: AI is now an ordinary, regulated part of medical care across U.S. hospitals and clinics.
events.caveats: The FDA notes the list is not comprehensive, and authorization does not by itself prove improved patient outcomes.

events.title: AI Model Disproves Erdős's 1946 Unit-Distance Conjecture
events.plainHeadline: AI disproved an 80-year-old conjecture from one of history's great mathematicians
events.organization: OpenAI; proof assessed by Alon, Bloom, Gowers, Litt, Sawin, Shankar, Tsimerman, Wang & Wood
events.summary: An internal OpenAI model disproved Paul Erdős's 1946 unit-distance conjecture in discrete geometry. A companion paper by nine prominent mathematicians assessed the argument; Fields Medalist Tim Gowers said he would have recommended it for the Annals of Mathematics.
events.whyItMatters: It is one of the clearest cases of AI producing genuinely new, research-level mathematics that top human experts have checked and endorsed.
events.caveats: The proof has not been formalized in Lean. Some other AI 'solutions' to Erdős problems turned out to rediscover existing proofs, so each result needs individual expert checking.

events.title: Machine-Verified Proof of the Riemann Hypothesis Found With AI
events.plainHeadline: A computer-checked proof of the 167-year-old Riemann Hypothesis was found with AI's help
events.organization: Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) with Claude; verified by Lean FRO & Mathlib Initiative
events.summary: Mathematician Levent Alpöge, working with Claude, released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis (and the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions) as ~17 million lines of Lean 4 code. The Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative stated that both the statement and the proof are correct, and MIT's Andrew Sutherland independently rebuilt and checked it.
events.whyItMatters: The Riemann Hypothesis, posed in 1859, is one of the seven $1M Millennium Prize problems and underpins our understanding of prime numbers. A machine-checked proof means a computer has confirmed every logical step.
events.caveats: No human-readable proof exists yet and no one yet understands why it works; it is not peer reviewed and the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as active. Mathematicians such as Maksym Radziwill and Kevin Buzzard have urged caution.

erdos.kpiSub: Erdős problems database (Terence Tao's group); AI tally frozen June 30, 2026
erdos.note: Status counts from teorth/erdosproblems problems.yaml (Nov 24, 2026): 587 solved (339 proved, 144 disproved, 104 resolved otherwise) and 634 open-type. 'Solved with AI' = full resolutions listed in the AI-contributions wiki as AI standalone (18) or AI collaborating with humans (36), 52 distinct problems; it excludes 37 cases where AI only found an existing solution, 14 later found to have prior solutions, and partial results. The wiki stopped updating June 30, 2026 and erdosproblems.com stopped showing solved counts Oct 6, 2026; the wiki warns it is 'not a benchmark' and has selection bias.

famous.name: Riemann Hypothesis
famous.detail: Lean-only proof by Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) with Claude; 175,187 modules checked with standard axioms by independent groups (Waterloo, MIT). No human-readable proof yet; Clay still lists it as active.

famous.name: Navier–Stokes
famous.detail: Alpöge & Buckmaster claim unforced 3D blowup with heavy AI assistance; its numerical certificate is not yet released. An earlier OpenAI 'forced' result (Sep 2026) was disputed as the wrong problem.

famous.name: Yang–Mills mass gap
famous.detail: An OpenAI submission (Oct 2026) shows existence only, not a mass gap, per a review group chaired by David Gross.

famous.name: Hodge conjecture
famous.detail: OpenAI claims an unreviewed special case; it withdrew three related papers over a sign error.

famous.name: Birch & Swinnerton-Dyer
famous.detail: OpenAI claims an unreviewed partial result.

famous.name: Poincaré conjecture
famous.detail: Proved by Grigori Perelman; the only Millennium problem solved so far.

famous.name: Erdős unit-distance conjecture
famous.detail: Disproved by an OpenAI model; checked by external mathematicians including Alon, Bloom and Gowers.

famous.name: VP ≠ VNP (algebraic P vs NP)
famous.detail: Anthropic and OpenAI each posted Lean proofs; Anthropic says no human mathematician has checked it. Does not settle P vs NP.

famous.name: Exponential Time Hypothesis
famous.detail: OpenAI and Anthropic claim to refute it with Lean proofs; experts say this is not yet certification of the claim.

mathTracker.recentClaimsNote: Nov 23–25, 2026: OpenAI posted VP ≠ VNP plus nine more manuscripts (e.g. matrix-multiplication exponent, Smale's 9th problem, polynomial Hirsch conjecture) and Google Research posted about nine 'Cogentic' papers (e.g. factoring, discrete logs). All are self-reported and not yet peer reviewed; OpenAI's repository notes some 'could have issues'.

openMathProblems.name: Riemann Hypothesis
openMathProblems.aiRole: Mathematician Levent Alpöge (Anthropic) found a proof working with Claude, delivered as ~17 million lines of Lean 4 code (also covering the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions).
openMathProblems.latestMilestone: Nov 20, 2026: proof posted. Nov 21: the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative stated that both the statement and the proof are correct, checked against Mathlib's own Riemann Hypothesis statement; MIT's Andrew Sutherland independently rebuilt all 175,187 modules using only Lean's standard axioms.
openMathProblems.caveat: No human-readable proof exists yet, it is not peer reviewed, and the Clay Mathematics Institute still lists the problem as active. Mathematicians including Maksym Radziwill and Kevin Buzzard stress that no one yet understands why the proof works.

openMathProblems.name: VP ≠ VNP & P ≠ NP
openMathProblems.status: VP ≠ VNP Proof Claimed (Unreviewed) · P vs NP Open
openMathProblems.aiRole: Nov 23, 2026: Anthropic posted a 70-page proof of VP ≠ VNP over every field, written by an internal Claude model, with a Lean 4 formalization; OpenAI posted its own VP ≠ VNP manuscript and Lean code hours later.
openMathProblems.latestMilestone: Anthropic's Lean proof compiles and is re-checked by a second proof kernel, but Anthropic states that no human mathematician has checked it and that machines cannot confirm the formal statement says exactly what is claimed.
openMathProblems.caveat: Unreviewed by independent experts and not peer reviewed. It does not settle P vs NP, which remains open.

openMathProblems.name: Erdős Open Problems (1,000+ Conjectures)
openMathProblems.aiRole: LLM reasoning + Lean 4 auto-formalization assisting mathematicians in verifying proofs, finding counterexamples, and uncovering forgotten solutions.
openMathProblems.latestMilestone: Hundreds of Erdős problems are now cataloged and formalized on erdosproblems.com, with AI-assisted Lean proofs contributing to multiple recent status changes.
openMathProblems.caveat: Human mathematicians remain essential to verify that formal statements actually match Erdős's intended mathematical meaning.

openMathProblems.name: Fermat's Last Theorem — Full Lean 4 Formalization
openMathProblems.aiRole: Imperial College London (Kevin Buzzard) & global Lean community formalizing Wiles's proof—creating the training ground for research-grade AI theorem provers.
openMathProblems.latestMilestone: Major structural blueprints and algebraic geometry prerequisites are actively compiling in Lean 4 under a 5-year EPSRC-funded roadmap.
openMathProblems.caveat: Fermat's Last Theorem was proven by Andrew Wiles in 1994; this project formally machine-verifies every line from axioms so AI can operate at modern research math depth.

openMathProblems.name: Busy Beaver BB(5) = 47,176,870
openMathProblems.aiRole: Automated deciders + complete Lean 4 formal proof resolved a 40-year-old problem in computability theory.
openMathProblems.latestMilestone: Completed July 2024; community has now moved on to BB(6) and formalizing decider pipelines.
openMathProblems.caveat: BB(6) contains Collatz-like 'antihydra' machines likely independent of simple proof systems.

openMathProblems.name: Fast Matrix Multiplication & Kissing Numbers
openMathProblems.aiRole: AlphaTensor (2022) and AlphaEvolve (2025) broke 50+ year-old algorithmic records and improved 11D kissing-number lower bounds.
openMathProblems.latestMilestone: 48 multiplications for 4×4 complex matrices (beating 1969 Strassen's 49) and 593 spheres in 11D kissing number.
openMathProblems.caveat: The ultimate asymptotic matrix-multiplication exponent ω (whether ω = 2) remains an open problem.
